messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: escalation policy 'oncall-sre' -> primary timed out, paging secondary (Jordan L). Incident ID: INC-2026-8743. Severity: SEV2. Acknowledgement window: 5m.

pagerduty: PagerDuty note: page sent to Jordan L, escalation to manager in 8m if no ack. Link: https://pd.example/INC-2026-8743

Sam W: I'm on laptop, pinging Jordan in thread. Jordan, can you ack?

Jordan L: seeing the page now, mobile was on DND — acked. Picking up.

Priya R: thanks. quick context: EU inference nodes started returning 500 errors ~10:32 UTC, error rate ~3.8% on production inference gateway for model redwood-mini-1. Customer-facing errors reported by support.

Jordan L: checking infra. tailing logs on gateway-prod-eu:
```
2026-03-14T10:33:02Z ERROR inference.gateway request_id=abc123 status=500 path=/v1/generate backend=runtime-4
2026-03-14T10:33:04Z WARN runtime-4 kv-cache-miss seq_len=512
```

Nidhi S: i'm looking at autoscaler metrics — GPU pool for eu-dedicated dipped, pods in CrashLoopBackOff (OOMKill). Could be memory blowup after a model rollout earlier.

Alex G: we rolled a quantized model variant to eu yesterday at 02:00. Could be regression with quantized kernels. Can we revert the rollout for EU traffic?

Jordan L: initiating canary rollback for model:redwood-mini-1@v2 -> routing back to v1 for eu region. Running command: `infractl rollout revert --region eu --model redwood-mini-1 --to v1`

Sam W: also disable batching heuristic that was turned on for v2 (batch_size_hint=2048). That caused memory spikes. Patch: `shardsctl set-config --region eu batching.batch_size_hint 512`

Priya R: opening a private incident channel: #inc-2918765432 (created). Summarize customer impact for status page: ~4% requests 500, affects EU customers using embeddings and chat short calls. No data leak.

incident-bot: command accepted, created channel #inc-2918765432, added oncall and SRE.

Jordan L: rollback started — routing change completed, new traffic routing to v1 at 10:38 UTC. Monitoring.

Nidhi S: pods are stabilizing, OOM count dropping. Node memory pressure clearing.

Support Ops: we have two escalations from customers, CS queued for notifications. Will post customer-facing ETA after mitigation.

Alex G: running load test sweep to validate: `loadtester --target https://eu.api.redwood.io/v1/generate --qps 100 --model redwood-mini-1@v1`

Jordan L: preliminary metrics: error rate fell from 3.8% -> 0.6% within 3 minutes of rollback. Latency normalizing.

Priya R: good. Are there any lingering degraded endpoints (embeddings)?

Nidhi S: embeddings endpoint showed minor spike but returned to baseline. I'll keep autoscaler at +1 buffer for 10m.

Sam W: thanks Jordan and Nidhi. Going to mark primary incident steps in the runbook. Suggest follow-up: revert quantized kernels for v2 until we can reproduce locally.

Jordan L: ack — updating incident timeline. Creating a postmortem placeholder and assigning owners: Alex -> model rollback investigation, Nidhi -> autoscaler/oom root cause, Sam -> customer comms.

PagerDuty: PagerDuty note: primary (Sam W) previously on-call timed out triggering secondary (Jordan L) — no manager escalation fired as secondary acked within window.

Priya R: quick note for status page: Customers may see intermittent 500 errors between 10:32-10:38 UTC, mitigation applied, full service recovered by 10:41 UTC. Draft status: "We experienced elevated error rates for inference requests in our EU region between 10:32 and 10:41 UTC due to a recent model rollout; traffic was routed back to the prior model version and service recovered. No customer data was exposed."

Support Ops: posting the drafted message now.

Sam W: handing off to follow-up owners. Jordan — if you want to stay on the postmortem, keep this thread updated, otherwise I'll close the incident channel in 2h.

Jordan L: I'll stay on the postmortem. Closing the active mitigation. Leaving notes: rollback, disable batching hint, increase autoscaler buffer, schedule model profiling.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-8743 moved to status: monitoring.

Sam W: closing notes: no manager escalation necessary. If PagerDuty policy needs tuning (e.g., mobile DND handling), file a policy tweak RFC.

Priya R: thanks team. Will post postmortem draft in #postmortems later today. :thumbsup:
